comments.body: Robert Sanderson, have you had a chance to actually try this interaction? Is there actually a concrete problem here, or is this more of an idea for a problem? [grin]

Just doing some testing and it appears that this is not allowed.

The error messages are horrible and should be fixed, but essentially as you don't have access to read /resource/to/attack, you can't reference it from your resource.

What I did

1. Standup webapp-plus with Webac enabled using mvn:jetty
2. Create a resource /resource/to/attack using user admin1
3. Ensure user user1 cannot read /resource/to/attack (OK)
3. Create a resource /allow/resource using user admin1
4. Create a WebAc Acl and WebAc Authorization attached to /allow/resource (auth.ttl attached)
5. Ensure that user user1 can read /allow/resource (OK) and can create a contained resource (OK)
6. Try to create an indirect container inside /allow/resource pointing to /resource/to/attack (indirect_expand.ttl attached)

> curl -i -XPUT -uuser1:password1 -H"Content-type: text/turtle" --data-binary "@indirect_expand.ttl" http://localhost:8080/rest/allow/resource/box
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Date: Thu, 07 Apr 2016 14:52:49 GMT
Link: <data:text/plain;base64,VW5hYmxlIHRvIGZpbmQgcmVmZXJlbmNlZCBub2RlClBlcm1pc3Npb24gZGVuaWVkIHRvIHBlcmZvcm0gYWN0aW9ucyAiW3JlZ2lzdGVyX25hbWVzcGFjZV0iIG9uIHBhdGggPHVua25vd24+>; rel="http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#constrainedBy"
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 108
Server: Jetty(9.3.1.v20150714)

Unable to find referenced node
Permission denied to perform actions "[register_namespace]" on path <unknown>

The register_namespace error I'll look into further, but I think the Unable to find referenced node is due to this each in the WebACRolesProvider.

Jared Whiklo One idea that occurred to me today for pulling in a second ACL (i.e., in addition to the ACL of the request resource) would be to use a request attribute to add the URIs of any additional resources that needs their ACLs retrieved and permissions parsed and added to the AuthorizationInfo. renderedFields.description:
In a thought experiment, it is anticipated that by manipulating direct and indirect containers, it would allow an attacker to create arbitrary triples on any resource that they should not have write access to.

For example, if a user can create an indirect container (/a):

/a a ldp:IndirectContainer ;
ldp:insertedContentRelation rdf:object ;
ldp:membershipResource /resource/to/attack ;
ldp:hasMemberRelation xxx:predicateToCreate .

When posting a new resource:
<> a rdf:Statement ;
rdf:object /resource/to/link

Would create the triple

/resource/to/attack xxx:predicateToCreate /resource/to/link

Expected Behavior:

The creation of the resource in the indirect container should fail with a permissions / auth related error.
